sentences.en: So I don't know if really cheap is true.
sentences.zh: 但我不知道“非常便宜”是不是真的。

sentences.en: But I saw they came out with, yeah, like, a Pentium processor that's, like, Arduino compatible.
sentences.zh: 不过我看到他们确实推出了一款奔腾处理器，而且是兼容 Arduino 的。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实是这样。

sentences.en: But people kind of passed over it because it's kind of not the point.
sentences.zh: 但人们似乎不太关注它，因为那并不是重点。

sentences.en: Like, it didn't make a lot of sense for people to do that.
sentences.zh: 对大家来说，那样做似乎没什么意义。

sentences.en: But the space is heating up.
sentences.zh: 不过这个领域正在升温。

sentences.en: Like, more and more people are making Arduino compatible boards.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的人开始制作兼容 Arduino 的开发板。

sentences.en: And the Arduino itself uses a basic microprocessor, which is only 8-bit computer and not that faSt.
sentences.zh: Arduino 本身使用的是基础微处理器，那只是一台 8 位计算机，速度并不快。

sentences.en: But now there's ones with, like, 32-bit computers running, you know, significantly faster where you can do, you know, a lot more processing on them versus just, like,
sentences.zh: 但现在有了 32 位计算机，运行速度快得多，你可以在上面做更多处理，而不只是像……

sentences.en: I'm going to blink some LEDs.
sentences.zh: 我只是要让 LED 灯闪烁一下。

sentences.en: Yeah, right.
sentences.zh: 是啊，没错。

sentences.en: No, the Arduino doesn't can do a lot more than that, but yeah.
sentences.zh: 不，Arduino 能做的远不止这些，但确实如此。

sentences.en: Yeah, but no, definitely nothing like a Raspberry Pi or, like, this Intel chip where you can do some serious, like, image processing or signal processing.
sentences.zh: 是啊，但它绝对比不上树莓派（Raspberry Pi）或英特尔这款芯片，后者可以进行一些严肃的图像处理或信号处理。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So if you were going to do image processing and you created a startup to do that, you might be doomed.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你打算做图像处理并为此创办一家公司，你可能就注定要失败了。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So my article is pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 所以我那篇文章挺有意思的。

sentences.en: The title is Why the World's Best Photo Startup is Going Out of Business.
sentences.zh: 标题是《为什么世界上最好的照片初创公司倒闭了》。

sentences.en: Went out of business.
sentences.zh: 已经倒闭了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: It's called The Government.
sentences.zh: 它叫“政府”。

sentences.en: So I think that this article is, like, phenomenally interesting.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这篇文章非常引人入胜。

sentences.en: It's on this app-based company called EverPix.
sentences.zh: 它讲的是一家叫 EverPix 的应用公司。

sentences.en: And the idea here is they would take your photos, you know, upload them to their cloud,
sentences.zh: 他们的理念是获取你的照片，上传到云端，

sentences.en: and then run whatever sort of image processing, classification, et cetera, to categorize your photos.
sentences.zh: 然后运行各种图像处理、分类等程序来整理你的照片。

sentences.en: And so then give you sort of a search engine for your photos.
sentences.zh: 从而为你提供一个照片搜索引擎。

sentences.en: You can say, you know, Eiffel Tower, and it would just show you photos that you might have taken over several years, over several trips to Paris of the Eiffel Tower.
sentences.zh: 你可以输入“埃菲尔铁塔”，它就会显示你过去几年去巴黎旅行时拍的所有埃菲尔铁塔的照片。

sentences.en: So it seems like a cool idea and actually was a good idea.
sentences.zh: 这听起来是个很酷的想法，实际上也确实是个好点子。

sentences.en: So, yeah, they had a small but very loyal fan base or, I guess, customer base that were paying customers.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有一个小而忠实的粉丝群，或者说付费客户群。

sentences.en: So, you know, they did have revenue.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们确实有收入。

sentences.en: And, you know, the too-long-don't-read summary is that they basically went out of business.
sentences.zh: 长话短说，他们基本上就是倒闭了。

sentences.en: So for two reasons.
sentences.zh: 原因有两个。

sentences.en: One is they didn't try to grow their product.
sentences.zh: 第一，他们没有尝试去扩大产品规模。

sentences.en: So they spent a lot of time focusing on the details and, you know, going through feedback from customers, fixing bugs.
sentences.zh: 他们花了很多时间关注细节，处理客户反馈，修复漏洞。

sentences.en: And they felt like, you know, the path forward was through, you know, pleasing their current customers as much as possible,
sentences.zh: 他们觉得前进的道路就是尽可能满足现有客户，

sentences.en: which, you know, is very noble and, you know, I can totally empathize with that.
sentences.zh: 这当然很高尚，我也完全能理解。

sentences.en: But meanwhile, you know, Instagram and Snapchat and these other major blockbuster, you know, photo-based apps spend more of their time growing the user base.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，Instagram、Snapchat 以及其他那些热门的照片类应用，把更多时间花在了扩大用户群上。

sentences.en: You know, log in with Facebook, get your friends to sign in, you know, more storage space if you get your friends to sign in.
sentences.zh: 比如通过 Facebook 登录，邀请朋友注册，邀请朋友注册还能获得更多存储空间。

sentences.en: They made the app free.
sentences.zh: 他们把应用做成了免费的。

sentences.en: I'm talking about their competitors.
sentences.zh: 我说的是他们的竞争对手。

sentences.en: And so they kind of left this company in the duSt.
sentences.zh: 所以他们把这家公司远远甩在了后面。

sentences.en: The other interesting thing is this was a startup, a few guys who were living in San Francisco, and they paid themselves each $200,000 a year cash salaries.
sentences.zh: 另一个有趣的地方是，这是一家初创公司，几个住在旧金山的家伙，他们给自己开出了每年 20 万美元的现金薪水。

sentences.en: And this raised a huge stink, you know, both in the article and in the comments.
sentences.zh: 这引起了轩然大波，无论是在文章里还是评论区。

sentences.en: There's a really interesting discussion going back and forth.
sentences.zh: 大家对此展开了非常有趣的讨论。

sentences.en: But it really makes you think, you know, if you have, I mean, this startup, you know, based on, you know, what I read in the article, they would have failed anyways.
sentences.zh: 但这确实让人深思，根据我读到的文章，这家初创公司无论如何都会失败的。

sentences.en: So it's like at least they were able to make a decent salary.
sentences.zh: 所以至少他们还能拿到不错的薪水。

sentences.en: But then on the flip side of it, or I guess a great salary, I should say.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，或者说应该说是高薪。

sentences.en: But on the flip side of it, you know, a lot of people are saying, look, you took, you got $8 million in funding, and you basically took most of it and kept it.
sentences.zh: 但反过来说，很多人都在说，看，你们拿到了 800 万美元的融资，结果基本上把大部分钱都装进了自己口袋。

sentences.en: Like the investors should never invest in any company that you guys make, and they're just really upset, you know.
sentences.zh: 投资者永远不应该投资你们这些人创办的任何公司，大家真的很生气。

sentences.en: And so I thought that that whole dynamic was actually really interesting.
sentences.zh: 我觉得整个动态过程真的很有意思。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I never had heard of this before, this article, but this startup ever picks.
sentences.zh: 是啊，在读这篇文章之前我从没听说过 EverPix 这家初创公司。

sentences.en: But, yeah, I mean, I thought that was interesting, too, like when I was skimming the article the first time I saw it, and I saw the salary costs were like so huge.
sentences.zh: 不过，我第一次浏览文章看到薪资成本那么高时，也觉得很有意思。

sentences.en: And I was like, not just like theirs, but like in general, they were showing like how much they had spent on salaries.
sentences.zh: 我不只是说他们，而是说他们展示了在薪水上花了多少钱。

sentences.en: And I was like, wow, that's like really high.
sentences.zh: 我当时就想，哇，这真的太高了。

sentences.en: And as they were saying, like, oh, we're paying ourselves the equivalent, you know, of other jobs.
sentences.zh: 他们说，哦，我们拿的薪水和其他工作相当。

sentences.en: But that's kind of one of the things I've always heard about startups saying is like you don't take an equivalent salary.
sentences.zh: 但我一直听说初创公司的情况是，你不能拿同等的薪水。

sentences.en: You get a lot less salary because you're essentially donating some portion of your salary to the company in hopes that like, or you're investing it, right?
sentences.zh: 你的薪水要少得多，因为你本质上是在向公司捐赠一部分薪水，或者说是在投资，对吧？

sentences.en: So like instead of taking the money out now, you're leaving that money for the company to have more runway to get to the time when it makes tons of money.
sentences.zh: 所以与其现在把钱拿走，不如把钱留给公司，让它有更多的运营资金，直到公司开始赚大钱的时候。

sentences.en: And then your investment of shares and percentage ownership of the company pays out that much more.
sentences.zh: 然后你持有的股份和公司所有权比例带来的回报会更多。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, it's true that they had this growth issue where they were charging customers and it was hard to get new customers.
sentences.zh: 他们确实存在增长问题，因为他们向客户收费，很难获得新客户。

sentences.en: But, you know, if they had paid themselves like $50,000 a year instead of $200,000 a year, then maybe they'd have another year or two to sort that out.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们每年给自己发 5 万美元而不是 20 万美元，也许他们还能再撑一两年去解决问题。

sentences.en: But instead, they're just like, you know, they're dead now.
sentences.zh: 但现在，他们彻底没戏了。

sentences.en: So I think you have the next news article.
sentences.zh: 我想该轮到下一篇新闻了。

sentences.en: So, yeah, 3D printers at the Consumer Electronics Show.
sentences.zh: 好的，消费电子展（CES）上的 3D 打印机。

sentences.en: Oh, is that what that is?
sentences.zh: 哦，那是那个展会吗？

sentences.en: CES stands for it.
sentences.zh: CES 就是那个缩写。

sentences.en: Yeah, I never actually looked it up.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我从没查过。

sentences.en: I think it's Consumer Electronics Show.
sentences.zh: 我想应该是消费电子展。

sentences.en: So I'm not super big into consumer electronics, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我对消费电子产品不太感冒。

sentences.en: Like some people are or whatever, like the latest phones and the latest gadgets.
sentences.zh: 不像有些人那样，对最新的手机和各种小玩意儿很着迷。

sentences.en: But it's somewhat interesting.
sentences.zh: 但它还是有点意思的。

sentences.en: And I am interested in 3D printers.
sentences.zh: 我对 3D 打印机很感兴趣。

sentences.en: And there was a lot of news about 3D printers at this year's CES.
sentences.zh: 今年的 CES 上有很多关于 3D 打印机的新闻。

sentences.en: And, you know, I was trying to read through what people were saying.
sentences.zh: 我试着阅读了大家的评论。

sentences.en: And it's still like, I guess, a relatively young or new industry about what's going to happen with 3D printers.
sentences.zh: 我觉得 3D 打印机行业还处于相对年轻或新兴的阶段，未来会怎样还不好说。

sentences.en: And it appeals to me because a lot of hardware, a lot of software, and you get to make cool things that you hold in the end.
sentences.zh: 它吸引我的地方在于，它结合了硬件和软件，而且最终你能做出实实在在的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, definitely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But there's still like a lot of questions around my mind.
sentences.zh: 但我心里还有很多疑问。

sentences.en: Like I still see like a lot of people who think that they will be able to have a lot of use out of 3D printers without doing any CAD work.
sentences.zh: 我还是看到很多人认为，即使完全不懂 CAD，也能从 3D 打印机中获得很多用途。

sentences.en: Like no designing their own things in 3D prograMs.
sentences.zh: 比如不需要在 3D 程序中设计自己的东西。

sentences.en: And maybe that's like 3D programs need to become much easier to use.
sentences.zh: 也许 3D 程序需要变得更容易使用才行。

sentences.en: Or like this year there was a lot of scanners coming out.
sentences.zh: 或者像今年出现了许多扫描仪。

sentences.en: Like you could scan an everyday object like in your house.
sentences.zh: 你可以扫描家里的日常用品。

sentences.en: Like, oh, I like this mug.
sentences.zh: 比如，哦，我喜欢这个杯子。

sentences.en: I'm going to scan this mug and then I'll have a 3D model of it.
sentences.zh: 我要扫描这个杯子，然后我就有了它的 3D 模型。

sentences.en: So maybe that's one avenue.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能是一条途径。

sentences.en: But they also have the Thingiverse, right?
sentences.zh: 但他们也有 Thingiverse，对吧？

sentences.en: At least the Thingomatic has the Thingiverse.
sentences.zh: 至少 Thingomatic 有 Thingiverse。

sentences.en: And it's like a huge warehouse of 3D objects.
sentences.zh: 那是一个巨大的 3D 对象仓库。

sentences.en: Like I've done that before, just printed other people's objects.
sentences.zh: 我以前也做过，就是打印别人的模型。

sentences.en: But how far does that get you?
sentences.zh: 但这能走多远呢？

sentences.en: Like if you had bought like your own 3D printer in your house and you didn't know any like programming, any, you know, didn't want to do any CAD work, 3D work,
sentences.zh: 如果你在家里买了一台 3D 打印机，却不懂任何编程，也不想做任何 CAD 或 3D 设计工作，

sentences.en: like would you justify the price like of $1,000 to only be able to print stuff that's on Thingiverse?
sentences.zh: 你觉得花 1000 美元买它，只为了打印 Thingiverse 上的东西，这值得吗？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, so the thing is like the only if the printing itself was an activity.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，除非打印本身就是一种乐趣。

sentences.en: Like if I would get my son when he's older and the two of us would find crazy things on the Internet, like on Thingiverse, like dinosaurs or whatever, and print them out.
sentences.zh: 比如等我儿子大一点，我们俩一起在网上找些疯狂的东西，比如 Thingiverse 上的恐龙之类的，然后打印出来。

sentences.en: But yeah, you're right.
sentences.zh: 但你说得对。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm hoping that by then the price will be more like, you know, $300 or something.
sentences.zh: 我希望到那时价格能降到 300 美元左右。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So they have $300 ones now, but they tend to involve more tinkering.
sentences.zh: 现在确实有 300 美元的，但往往需要更多的折腾。

sentences.en: Oh, bummer.
sentences.zh: 哦，真扫兴。

sentences.en: So I think, yeah, maybe in another few years it will be.
sentences.zh: 我想，也许再过几年就可以了。

sentences.en: I just like, I just wonder like what is, and several of the articles talked about this and the one that will be in the show notes was more lengthy than most,
sentences.zh: 我只是好奇，几篇文章都谈到了这一点，其中一篇放在节目说明里的文章比大多数文章都要详尽，

sentences.en: but you still need the killer app.
sentences.zh: 但你仍然需要一个“杀手级应用”。

sentences.en: Like what is the thing that you want to get a 3D printer to, like you would do it, get one just to do that.
sentences.zh: 就是那种让你非买不可的理由。

sentences.en: And we haven't really found that yet.
sentences.zh: 我们还没找到那个理由。

sentences.en: And maybe once we do, it'll be like, oh, of course, like this is awesome.
sentences.zh: 也许一旦找到了，大家就会觉得，哦，当然，这太棒了。

sentences.en: But for now, I'm still interested because like I like electronics and tinkering and I'm not afraid to do 3D drawing.
sentences.zh: 但目前，我感兴趣是因为我喜欢电子产品和折腾，也不怕做 3D 绘图。

sentences.en: But like the whole it's ready for the masses or it's going prime time or it's a consumer device still eludes me.
sentences.zh: 但关于它是否已经准备好进入大众市场，或者成为主流消费设备，我还是持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: Like I'm not sure that that makes any sense.
sentences.zh: 我不确定这是否有意义。

sentences.en: Maybe the 3D printer becomes like a way for you to customize, you know, something where like, you know, you'd go to Best Buy and you would buy like a toaster, let's say.
sentences.zh: 也许 3D 打印机可以成为一种定制方式，比如你去百思买（Best Buy）买个烤面包机，

sentences.en: But it would just give you like the inside of the toaster.
sentences.zh: 它只给你烤面包机的内部零件。

sentences.en: And then you could go to Thingiverse and the toaster manufacturing company has given you like 100 different shells
sentences.zh: 然后你可以去 Thingiverse，烤面包机制造商为你提供了 100 种不同的外壳，

sentences.en: for the toaster, like one that looks like an Angry Bird or whatever.
sentences.zh: 比如愤怒的小鸟造型之类的。

sentences.en: And you could just print whatever you wanted.
sentences.zh: 你可以打印任何你想要的。

sentences.en: Oh, Angry Bird toaster.
sentences.zh: 哦，愤怒的小鸟烤面包机。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What I've always wanted.
sentences.zh: 我一直想要的。

sentences.en: Actually, you know, I think 3D printing something like a toaster is probably supremely dangerous.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我觉得用 3D 打印机打印烤面包机之类的东西可能极其危险。

sentences.en: Well, and a bad idea because it's plastic, it'll melt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且是个坏主意，因为它是塑料做的，会融化。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 你说得太对了。

sentences.en: But you know what I mean.
sentences.zh: 但你明白我的意思。

sentences.en: I mean, you get where I'm going with this.
sentences.zh: 你懂我说的方向。

sentences.en: But I mean, even in that case, like I agree, like I think 3D printing rapid prototyping has like a use in industry and among engineers and like for rapid prototyping, right?
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，我也同意，我认为 3D 打印和快速原型制作在工业和工程师群体中确实有用途，对吧？

sentences.en: Or like at a store, like the Best Buy, you would go buy the, they would have a kit of toaster oven innards.
sentences.zh: 或者在商店里，比如百思买，他们卖烤面包机的核心组件。

sentences.en: But instead of stocking 300 different styles of toaster oven, they would just stock one or two different insides.
sentences.zh: 与其库存 300 种不同风格的烤面包机，他们只需要库存一两种内部零件。

sentences.en: And then they would 3D print whichever one you chose.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会 3D 打印你选择的外壳。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: But that doesn't still explain like why I would need one at home.
sentences.zh: 但这还是不能解释为什么我家里需要一台。

sentences.en: Unless I was going to like change toaster shells every couple of months.
sentences.zh: 除非我打算每隔几个月就换一次烤面包机的外壳。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: But, you know, maybe that's, maybe that's where it goes.
sentences.zh: 但也许，也许这就是未来的方向。

sentences.en: Like for example, you know, you don't really need a paint mixer at home.
sentences.zh: 比如，你家里其实并不需要一台油漆搅拌机。

sentences.en: But, you know, I'm really happy when, you know, I go to Lowe's and they have one.
sentences.zh: 但当我去劳氏（Lowe's）看到他们有的时候，我真的很开心。

sentences.en: But paint mixers aren't all talked about at CES and people saying, oh, this is the wave of the future.
sentences.zh: 但没人会在 CES 上谈论油漆搅拌机，也没人说这是未来的趋势。

sentences.en: Well, maybe they were.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许他们谈过。

sentences.en: Maybe they were at CES 1932.
sentences.zh: 也许在 1932 年的 CES 上谈过。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Anyways, 3D printers are cool.
sentences.zh: 总之，3D 打印机很酷。

sentences.en: I guess my point is maybe it's not, you know, the end goal really isn't your home.

sentences.zh: 对于不知道的人，Glassdoor 是一个讨论相关信息的网站，它的运作方式是你可以浏览 Glassdoor，

sentences.en: and they'll give you, like, superficial information on different jobs, different companies, salary, expectation, things like that.
sentences.zh: 他们会提供关于不同工作、不同公司、薪资、期望值等方面的表面信息。

sentences.en: But then after you get a certain, you know, way through the site, they say, oh, hey, you know, you have to give a little to take a little more.

sentences.en: And so they have you log in through, like, their account or Facebook, et cetera, and put in some anonymous statistics about your job.

sentences.en: Which, you know, they use to sort of, you know, keep the whole thing running.

sentences.zh: 每年他们都会评选最佳雇主、最疯狂的工作环境等等。

sentences.en: And this is a top 25 oddball questions.
sentences.zh: 而这篇是 25 个最奇葩的问题。

sentences.en: And it's, you know, a lot of, I've seen a lot of, you know, sites like this.

sentences.en: And most of them focus on questions that they ask, like project managers, on the grounds that you need to be able to sort of think critically and think mathematically.
sentences.zh: 它们大多关注的是问项目经理的那类问题，理由是你需要具备批判性思维和数学思维能力。

sentences.en: So you see a lot of these, like, this one in particular says, how many cows are in Canada?
sentences.zh: 所以你会看到很多这样的问题，比如这一条：加拿大有多少头牛？

sentences.en: How many quarters would you need to reach the height of the Empire State Building?
sentences.zh: 你需要多少个 25 美分硬币才能达到帝国大厦的高度？

sentences.en: You know, I've heard, like, how many ping pong balls can you fill in an airplane, stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 我还听过类似“一架飞机能装多少个乒乓球”之类的问题。

sentences.en: Those are all the same type of question.
sentences.zh: 这些都是同一类问题。

sentences.en: Or how much extra gasoline would the United States consume if there was a law passed that all headlights had to be on all the time on cars when they were driving?
sentences.zh: 或者，如果法律规定汽车行驶时必须全天候开启前大灯，美国会多消耗多少汽油？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And most of the time what it comes down to is you have this, like, very complex dynamical system.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候，归根结底你面对的是一个非常复杂的动态系统。

sentences.en: And you just need to start with, like, trying to simplify it as much as you can.
sentences.zh: 你只需要从尽可能简化它开始。

sentences.en: And, you know, just like, for example, the ping pong question, you start by thinking, you know, how many ping pong balls can you fit in, like, a one meter cube?
sentences.zh: 比如那个乒乓球的问题，你先思考一立方米的空间能装多少个乒乓球？

sentences.en: Yeah, like, basically it's just all about estimation.
sentences.zh: 没错，基本上就是估算的问题。

sentences.en: But it also proves on some of them you need to know a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 但也证明了在某些问题上，你需要了解更多知识。

sentences.en: Like, for instance, the one I said, like, headlights being on.
sentences.zh: 比如我刚才说的大灯开启的问题。

sentences.en: Like, that there's an inefficiency in powering a generator to have the headlight on that causes you to use more gas or whatever.
sentences.zh: 开启大灯需要发电机供电，这会产生效率损耗，导致你消耗更多汽油之类的。

sentences.en: In addition to estimating how many cars are in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这还需要估算美国有多少辆车。

sentences.en: and how much do they drive and how much gas do they consume.
sentences.zh: 以及它们行驶里程和油耗是多少。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: So, yeah, it's pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 所以，这挺酷的。

sentences.en: But you should be ready to answer those.
sentences.zh: 但你得准备好回答这些问题。

sentences.en: Like, if, like, that's a really common style of question.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常常见的面试风格。

sentences.en: The estimate something really big that there's no way you can actually know the answer to.
sentences.zh: 估算一些你根本不可能知道确切答案的庞大事物。

sentences.en: I don't think that's oddball.
sentences.zh: 我不觉得这算奇葩。

sentences.en: Like, I think you should really know that if you're going to do any sort of engineering interview.
sentences.zh: 我觉得如果你要参加任何工程类面试，这都是你应该掌握的。

sentences.en: Yeah, definitely don't just say, like, 100 or something like that.
sentences.zh: 没错，千万别只说“100”之类的数字。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, what they want to know, and we'll talk about this more as we go on, but what they really want to know are just, like, the process and, like, your methodology.
sentences.zh: 他们想知道的，我们稍后会深入讨论，但他们真正想看的是你的思考过程和方法论。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's it.
sentences.zh: 没错，我想就是这样。

sentences.en: Like, knowing you can take a seemingly impossible question and break it down piece by piece.
sentences.zh: 知道如何将一个看似不可能的问题拆解开来分析。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.zh: 那么，你读过这些问题了吗？

sentences.zh: 我猜这和它的弹跳方式有关，是为了防止它旋转之类的？

sentences.zh: 我其实以为是为了减速之类的。

sentences.zh: 哦，那是真正的答案吗？

sentences.en: So, on interviewing, what are some...
sentences.zh: 那么，关于面试，有哪些……

sentences.en: What's that?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: On interviewing, so, what are some, like, good tips for people, like, if they're going to interview?
sentences.zh: 关于面试，对于要去面试的人来说，有什么好的建议吗？

sentences.en: So, this is sort of deviating from the normal show.
sentences.zh: 这有点偏离我们平时的节目主题了。

sentences.en: Yeah, we're definitely going to get to Unix commands, but, as you might expect, you know,
sentences.zh: 没错，我们肯定会讲到 Unix 命令，但正如你所料，

sentences.en: that's not an entire language, although maybe it should be, but, you know, we wanted to add a little bit of spice,
sentences.zh: 那不是一门完整的语言，虽然也许应该如此，但我们想加点调料，

sentences.en: a little bit of interesting content, and so we decided to think, you know, what does it take to really ace an interview, right?
sentences.zh: 加点有趣的内容，所以我们决定探讨一下，怎样才能在面试中脱颖而出，对吧？

sentences.en: Now, of course, you have to know, you know, you have to know what you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 当然，你必须得懂行。

sentences.en: You can't have a degree in computer science and then try to ace an interview for the legal team, right?
sentences.zh: 你不能拿个计算机科学学位去应聘法律团队的职位，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it's just not going to happen.
sentences.zh: 那是不可能的。

sentences.en: But, you know, with that said, there are...
sentences.zh: 但话虽如此，确实有……

sentences.en: There's a whole process to interviewing and to being interviewed, and, you know, the reality is that, sadly enough,
sentences.zh: 面试和被面试有一整套流程，现实情况是，很遗憾，

sentences.en: there are some people who fail at that process, despite the fact that they're extremely qualified, and it works the other way as well.
sentences.zh: 有些人尽管资质极高，却在面试环节失败了，反之亦然。

sentences.en: And so understanding the interview process is a big step towards, you know, either, you know, changing careers or to interviewing other people for roles within your company.
sentences.zh: 所以了解面试流程是职业转型，或者为公司招聘人才的一大步。

sentences.en: Or graduating from college and trying to get your first job.
sentences.zh: 或者对于刚毕业想找第一份工作的人来说也是如此。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah, definitely.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错，绝对是。

sentences.en: There's no doubt.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: And we'll mostly be talking about...
sentences.zh: 我们主要会讨论……

sentences.en: We'll go from general to specific, but, like, in the beginning, it'll be applicable to everything,
sentences.zh: 我们会从一般性问题讲到具体问题，起初这些建议适用于所有面试，

sentences.en: but then further along, we'll start talking specifically if you have what's called a technical interview,
sentences.zh: 但稍后我们会专门讨论所谓的“技术面试”，

sentences.en: which is an interview where they're going to ask you to solve problems or, you know, do programming in the interview, which not every interview is that way.
sentences.zh: 也就是面试官要求你解决问题或进行编程的面试，并非所有面试都是这样。

sentences.en: And if possible, you should try to find out in advance if it will be a technical interview or not.
sentences.zh: 如果可能的话，你应该提前打听清楚是否会有技术面试。

sentences.en: Yeah, definitely.
sentences.zh: 没错，绝对的。

sentences.en: That's a really good point.
sentences.zh: 这观点很好。

sentences.en: It's kind of sad, but I considered college as a career.
sentences.zh: 有点可悲，但我曾把上大学当成一种职业。

sentences.en: Like, when I was thinking in my head switching careers, I guess it's because I was in college for so long.
sentences.zh: 当我考虑转行时，我想可能是因为我在大学待得太久了。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧。

sentences.en: It's pretty bad.
sentences.zh: 这挺糟糕的。

sentences.en: Anyways, so you want to go first?
sentences.zh: 总之，你想先说吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 好啊。

sentences.en: So, I mean, like, the first, and maybe this is, like, like I said, they're general and therefore probably more obvious in the beginning,
sentences.zh: 我是说，第一点，也许像我刚才说的，这些建议很通用，所以起初听起来可能比较显而易见，

sentences.en: but you should read up about the company you're interviewing with.
sentences.zh: 但你一定要提前了解你要面试的公司。

sentences.en: I mean, it's kind of, like, bad, but I've done interviews where the person comes in and is kind of like, so what do you guys do?
sentences.zh: 这听起来有点糟糕，但我面试过那种走进来问“你们到底是做什么的？”的人。

sentences.en: And they don't mean, like, what kind of work specifically do I do?
sentences.zh: 他们指的不是“我具体做什么工作？”，

sentences.en: Because I've already said that.
sentences.zh: 因为我已经说过了。

sentences.en: But they're, like, just asking, like, in general, what does the company do?
sentences.zh: 他们问的是公司总体上是做什么的。

sentences.en: Or, like, what products they make?
sentences.zh: 或者他们生产什么产品？

sentences.en: And it's like, okay, that's, like, you didn't look us up on the internet?
sentences.zh: 这感觉就像，你上网查过我们吗？

sentences.en: You know, like, this is not good.
sentences.zh: 这可不太好。

sentences.en: So definitely read up and know about, you know, like, what are the most famous products they do or the things in the news.
sentences.zh: 所以一定要提前阅读并了解他们最著名的产品或新闻动态。

sentences.en: And specifically, like, if it's a big company, it's good to find out, like, at that branch, what do they work on?
sentences.zh: 特别是如果是一家大公司，最好了解一下该分支机构具体负责什么业务。

sentences.en: So, like, if your company has, like, you know, makes furniture, and in one city they make couches and in one city they make desks.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你的公司制造家具，一个城市生产沙发，另一个城市生产书桌。

sentences.en: You know, if you can find that out, like, that's also more helpful because then if you're interviewing in the city where they make desks,
sentences.zh: 如果你能查到这些信息，会很有帮助，因为如果你是在生产书桌的城市面试，

sentences.en: you're probably talking to people who work on making desks.
sentences.zh: 你面对的可能就是负责书桌业务的人。

sentences.en: And then, you know, you can ask specifically about that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 这样你就可以针对性地询问相关问题。

sentences.en: Yeah, definitely.
sentences.zh: 没错，绝对的。

sentences.en: I mean, so Patrick and I have been interviewees several times.
sentences.zh: 我是说，Patrick 和我当过很多次面试者。

sentences.en: We've interviewed a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 我们也面试过很多人。

sentences.en: Probably between the two of us, we've interviewed over 150 people, just estimating.
sentences.zh: 估计我们俩加起来面试过超过 150 人。

sentences.en: So, and one of the big things is, you know, there's some people who are there, but they don't really want the job or, you know,
sentences.zh: 其中一个重点是，有些人虽然来了，但他们并不真的想要这份工作，或者，

sentences.en: they find out they don't want the job by the time they get to your interview, if they've had other prior interviews the same day.
sentences.zh: 如果他们当天还有其他面试，到你这里时他们可能已经发现自己并不想要这份工作了。

sentences.en: And so, as an interviewer, just because of the statistics, it's very easy to sort of lump someone into the pool of people
sentences.zh: 作为面试官，从统计学角度看，很容易把某人归入那类人中，

sentences.en: where you just feel like this, like they're just not interested, right?
sentences.zh: 就是那种让你觉得他们根本不感兴趣的人，对吧？

sentences.en: Because there are a lot of people who aren't interested but are interviewing for other reasons or who knows, right?
sentences.zh: 因为确实有很多人并不感兴趣，只是因为其他原因来面试，谁知道呢？

sentences.en: So, yeah, you definitely, as an interviewee, you want to understand the company and be enthusiastic.
sentences.zh: 所以，作为面试者，你一定要了解公司并表现出热情。

sentences.en: And, I mean, the reality is if you don't understand what that company does, then, like, how can you really want to work there?
sentences.zh: 说实话，如果你都不了解那家公司是做什么的，你怎么可能真的想在那里工作呢？

sentences.en: It doesn't really add up.
sentences.zh: 这逻辑不通。

sentences.en: But yet you find tons of people who are in that category.
sentences.zh: 但你还是会发现很多人属于这一类。

sentences.en: So, that's definitely where you want to do your homework.
sentences.zh: 所以，这绝对是你需要做功课的地方。

sentences.en: So, another one is it's really important to be confident and not to be intimidated.
sentences.zh: 另一个重点是，保持自信、不要被吓倒非常重要。

sentences.en: Or at least to act confident.
sentences.zh: 或者至少要表现得自信。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: Especially when you're doing a technical interview, just kind of keep telling yourself or just remember, meditate on this.
sentences.zh: 特别是在进行技术面试时，不断告诉自己，或者记住这一点，反复思考：

sentences.en: That, you know, the interviewer, you know, he might have asked that same question to, say, 50 other people, right?
sentences.zh: 面试官可能已经问过 50 个人同样的问题了，对吧？

sentences.en: Or if he hasn't, he's preparing to ask that question to another 20 or 30 people, right?
sentences.zh: 或者如果还没问过，他正准备问另外 20 到 30 个人，对吧？

sentences.en: So, he's going to be an expert on that question.
sentences.zh: 所以，他会是那个问题的专家。
